Title: Tiny World Model
Description:
Overview # After coming across Ha & Schmidhuber’s 2018 paper World Models earlier this year, I have been working on building a “tiny world model” on a clone of Chrome’s Dino game.
The final model is small: a variational autoencoder (VAE), a recurrent world model and a two-layer actor. Getting the three pieces to work together required many rounds of debugging. There were many mistakes along the way: plausible-looking images hid a broken latent representation, a weighted loss hid a data problem, and a controller kept improving in an imagined world while getting worse in the real one.

Title: Subagents and the Art of Spending More
Description:
I had a random discussion in my Telegram group about AI. I noticed that some of them had really high token usage and very long sessions. After some more discussion, I realised that they had fairly complex setups, with lots of coordination between their agents.
Like any other engineer on a weekend, I opened my laptop and fired up two separate Pi sessions to run the same task. One used no subagents and the other used subagents.
